subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk gain a batch STT backend seam now, and should the first non-Apple backend bridge to Gateway `tools.media.audio` rather than adding a macOS-only endpoint setting?
rationale: The source confirms the missing capability, but adding it creates new provider/auth/security and UX contracts that repository policy says need maintainer product and security direction before implementation.

options.title: Design batch PTT STT seam first
options.body: Keep Apple Speech as default, add a native batch-only PTT boundary, and route the first selectable backend through existing Gateway media-audio/provider security contracts.

options.title: Track only the broad ASR issue
options.body: Treat this request as a dependent slice of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661 and defer implementation until the cross-platform ASR decision lands.

options.title: Keep native PTT Apple-only
options.body: Decline configurable native PTT STT for now and ask users to use channel media-audio or plugin/provider paths outside the macOS capture pipeline.

recommendation.title: Design batch PTT STT seam first
recommendation.body: Keep Apple Speech as default, add a native batch-only PTT boundary, and route the first selectable backend through existing Gateway media-audio/provider security contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` has the strongest native macOS PTT/Talk history signal and owns the most relevant product/API boundary in the sampled files.
